title: Southern African bird communities followed about 28% of their spatial temperature gradient in 2008-2024 but only 2-5% of their rainfall gradient; waterbirds followed about one third
abstract: Question: campaign networks follow about 12% of their spatial temperature gradient in time, but all of them are in the Northern Hemisphere and test temperature only. Do southern African bird communities give the same small fraction, and do they follow rainfall instead? Data: Southern African Bird Atlas Project 2 (SABAP2, 2008-2024) and SABAP1 (1986-1992) via GBIF facet counts (CC BY 4.0); 113 one-degree cells, 3,534 cell-year-halves, 21.2 million records; CRU TS 4.09 temperature and rainfall. Method: cross-fitted species temperature and precipitation indices from 846 half-degree cells; record-weighted community temperature (CTI) and precipitation (CPI) indices; within-cell trend and anomaly slopes divided by the spatial slope (fraction 1 = full space-for-time equivalence); controls for month mix, effort, observer count and pentad location; year-effect variant; species-shuffle null; 2-degree block bootstrap. Results: CTI followed 0.28 (95% CI 0.06-0.51) of the spatial expectation for the 0.27 C/decade warming trend and 0.0 (-0.04 to 0.02) for year-to-year anomalies. With year effects (between-cell warming only) the fraction was 0.12 (-0.41 to 0.51). CPI followed only 0.027 (-0.001 to 0.047) of its spatial rainfall gradient within 12 months and 0.053 (0.008-0.092) within 24 months; land birds 0.021 (interval includes 0). Waterbirds followed 0.34 (0.18-0.66) within 24 months. Rainfall changed composition strongly (143 of 636 species with |z| > 3), but the species responses were not related to their rainfall niche (r = 0.04). SABAP1 to SABAP2 could not test temperature because cell warming was nearly uniform. Conclusion: the first Southern Hemisphere test gives a temperature trend fraction near Swedish birds and a zero year-to-year fraction; birds in this semi-arid region do not track rainfall more than heat, except waterbirds. Limitations: the trend fraction cannot be separated from slow atlas changes (effort doubled); detection/non-detection cards, not abundance; ad hoc lists not separable; niches from the same atlas.

display.caption: Fractions of the spatial gradient that SABAP2 bird communities followed in time (2008-2024), with 95% block-bootstrap intervals. Red: community temperature index (CTI) on temperature. Blue: community precipitation index (CPI) on rainfall. Dashed line: the 75-network trend fraction 0.12 (sci:sha256:0037934e).

Left and middle: CPI anomaly against the 24-month rainfall anomaly (deciles, within cell-half) for land birds and waterbirds; dashed line = full spatial equivalence. Right: species record-share response to rainfall against the species precipitation index (636 species, r = 0.04).
Mean cell-demeaned anomalies over 113 one-degree cells per half-year. Top: 12-month log rainfall and CPI. Bottom: 12-month temperature and CTI. CTI rose steadily, also in the cool 2021-2022 years.
